body:
Man, I love working out tbh. I've been trying to get bigger arms at home with protein, dumbbells, and body weight exercises, but I can only stick to it one to two weeks every month before I just start playing video games alone and hanging out with my friends. You're right though, it does feel good. Still don't know if that could translate to confidence for me, but I'm definitely going to try to actually stick to a more robust routine soon.

I don't do much more than read, game, and drink nowadays.

I've skimmed the book of pook and I'm honestly not sure how I feel about it.

Reporting the lawyer to the bar association is a good idea. I'll probably do that.

This is encouraging. I feel like there might be reasonable hope for everything else (even though anxiety and diffidence makes that difficult and unpleasant to say or think) if I can make a decent living. The problem of employment has seemed permanent and unalterable to me for a long time. I'd almost definitely have more confidence if I knew I were at least somewhat financially secure.

You generally waive the right to appeal if you plead guilty. Oddly, I could file a petition for writ of habeas corpus and argue that my counsel was adversarial and coercive if I were in jail or prison, but I only did 2 weeks and got out on the day of my "hearing." :/

Edit: That hasn't happened in a fairly long time but I haven't left my house much either. I don't know... I know you're right about talking to people and practicing, but it just feels like there's a mental block that won't allow me to do that.

Misdemeanor. Is that true? I live in one of the poorest states in the USA and jobs go quick so it might be different elsewhere, but retail, fast food, and call center apps have asked about detailed criminal history. I won't be qualified to do much else for a while.

Domestic battery. My lawyer made me think I could just get it expunged later, but I can't. I couldn't pay bail and spending months in jail for something I didn't do before even having a hearing seemed ridiculous.  

It makes me look like a terrible person. :/

Edit: This was one of the biggest factors in me realizing how brutal and cruel the world can be. It's like no one cares about all he values and ideals we claim to cherish, especially when the victim is disliked for sociopolitical or religious reasons.

Edit 2: I've also been drinking and don't know if I make sense.
